Evidence Recorded: This diff rewires 24 files that previously resolved the Superboss Register SQLite DB path via a hardcoded literal, a self-built os.path.join(), or an independent SUPERBOSS_REGISTER_DB re-read, so they all delegate to the single canonical resolver superboss-register.py's resolve_superboss_db_path() (exists/size/SQLite-header/umr_tasks-table validation, hard-fails via SuperbossDbPathError on a decoy/corrupt file), using the same lazy-import-cached _superboss_register()/_resolve_db_path() convention already proven in reconcile_stale_running_workers.py and worker-exit-status-bridge.py -- I independently confirmed both the resolver function and that precedent are real in the live /opt/veridian/scripts checkout, confirmed the resolver's CLI dispatch is correctly gated behind if __name__ == '__main__' so importlib exec_module has no side effects, and py_compile'd/bash -n'd all 24 changed files with zero syntax errors. directive_engine.py correctly threads the pre-existing VERIDIAN_DIRECTIVE_SUPERBOSS_DB test seam through resolve_superboss_db_path()'s default_path parameter rather than dropping it, and migrate_2026-07-31_dedup_constraints.py correctly resolves the path once in main() and threads it through _backup_db()/_write_lock() rather than re-resolving inconsistently. This diff is PR #357 on FChecklist/veridian-scripts (open, no existing CI checks or review comments), corresponding to already-committed local commit 9a1809d on branch fix/register-path-resolution-decoy-cleanup-umr20260813130245-6a26 -- verified NOT yet merged into origin/main, so this is genuine pending review work, not duplicate/already-landed work. No .github/workflows/** files are touched. Two real, but self-disclosed-in-the-commit-message, correctness caveats remain and should be weighed by the human sign-off: (1) several call sites (task-gateway.py's lookup_work_item/reverify_touched_knowledge_engine_rows, and generate_wiring_registry.py's load_capability_registry/_fetch_governance_tagged_knowledge_engine_rows/coverage_delta/build_from_knowledge_engine) dropped their prior 'if not os.path.isfile(DB_PATH): return None/[]/{}' graceful-degradation guard with no equivalent try/except for the resolver's new SuperbossDbPathError, so a genuinely missing/decoy DB now crashes those call sites instead of degrading gracefully -- likely the intended 'fail loud, not silent' behavior per the resolver's own documented design, but a real behavior change not yet independently verified against every real caller/cron schedule; (2) conversely, directive_engine.py, plan_generator.py, security-check.py, and prompt_gateway/gateway_persistence.py each already have a broad except-Exception (or similarly wide) wrapper around their DB call site that will silently swallow the new SuperbossDbPathError, meaning the intended hard-fail-on-decoy-DB protection for the underlying hazard this PR closes does not actually take effect at those four sites. Issues found: task-gateway.py (lookup_work_item, reverify_touched_knowledge_engine_rows) and generate_wiring_registry.py (load_capability_registry, _fetch_governance_tagged_knowledge_engine_rows, coverage_delta, build_from_knowledge_engine) removed their prior os.path.isfile(DB_PATH) short-circuit with no try/except for the new SuperbossDbPathError -- a missing/invalid DB now raises uncaught instead of gracefully returning None/[]/{} as before; needs confirmation this doesn't break any real caller or test harness that relies on graceful degradation.; directive_engine.py, plan_generator.py, security-check.py, and prompt_gateway/gateway_persistence.py each have a pre-existing broad except-Exception (or similarly wide) wrapper around their DB call site that will silently swallow resolve_superboss_db_path()'s new SuperbossDbPathError, so the decoy/corrupt-DB hard-fail protection this PR is meant to add does not actually surface at those four sites.; The identical ~15-line lazy-import _superboss_register()/_resolve_db_path() boilerplate is now duplicated verbatim across 24 files (following pre-existing precedent rather than introduced fresh here) -- a shared helper module would reduce drift risk if the loading convention ever needs to change, worth a follow-up cleanup rather than blocking this fix.
